mutants.before: const paid = piece.date && piece.date < stop ? piece.date : stop;
mutants.after: const paid = piece.date || piece.date < stop ? piece.date : stop;
mutants.line_text: const paid = piece.date && piece.date < stop ? piece.date : stop;
mutants.note: A dated piece after April 15 now keeps its own date, but `to` is then clipped to per.end, and the last period ends on April 15 (the same `stop`), so no day count changes; a null date still falls to `stop` because null < string is false. The existing test 'a payment after April 15 stops the count' passes with the mutant for this reason.

mutants.before: const to = paid < per.end ? paid : per.end;
mutants.after: const to = paid <= per.end ? paid : per.end;
mutants.line_text: const to = paid < per.end ? paid : per.end;
mutants.note: When paid equals per.end both branches give the same date, so `to` is unchanged.

real_defects.issue: Tax year 2024 (rates on file, so accepted without a warning about rates) was figured at days/365 in every rate period, though the 2024 Form 2210 worksheet divides the three 2024 periods by 366; the code only printed a 'may divide by 366' warning. It also summed a period's payments and rounded once, where line 4 is one rounded computation per payment. IRS Example 5 (2024): $6.56 + $26.67 = $33.23; the code gave $33.32. Fixed: each period divides by its calendar year's length and each entry is rounded; test from Example 5 and Table 2.

certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
